name: Lexical Abstractness Profile
description: Evaluates the depth of conceptual abstraction using word embeddings
mechanism: Rather than calculating a simple ratio, this method maps the entire text against high-dimensional word embeddings pre-trained on linguistic abstractness gradients. Large Language Models often maintain a uniformly moderate-to-high abstraction profile across the entire document to ensure broad applicability. Human writers, however, exhibit 'abstraction valleys'—deeply concrete sections of narrative or evidence that sharply contrast with their abstract introductions. By measuring the variance and depth of abstraction scores across the text's vector space, this method identifies the suspiciously 'smooth' abstraction profile typical of LLMs.
parameters:
Analysis type: Vector space embeddings
Media: Text
Input: Formatted text
Minimum length: 100 words
Output: Abstraction homogeneity score (0-100)
Processing: Embedding projection
accuracy: High — 75-85%. Particularly effective on long-form content where the structural pacing of human writing diverges sharply from AI generation.
source: Computational linguistics and semantic embedding analysis.
useCase: Detecting homogenously abstract text generated by AI models that fail to dynamically shift between theoretical arguments and highly concrete, grounded narratives.
strengths:
• Detects subtle, structural differences beyond vocabulary
• Highly effective at catching 'smooth', generalized narrative flows
• Robust against simple prompt-based evasion
limitations:
• Requires significant processing capability for embeddings
• Less effective on extremely short texts (under 100 words)
• Heavily dependent on the quality of the baseline embedding model

references.title: Turney, P. D., et al. (2011). Lexical entailment and abstractness. Natural Language Engineering.
Bhatia, Bhatia, & Momennejad (2020). The abstract representations of LLMs vs Humans.
